expectations.text: Uses the hazard analysis structure: steps and ingredients, identify biological/chemical/physical hazards, decide whether each requires a preventive control, and justify each decision
expectations.evidence: Ingredient and step tables with hazard, 'reasonably foreseeable? justification', HRPC? and control columns

expectations.text: Considers foreseeable use: consumers eating the dough raw, so pathogens in flour (E. coli/Salmonella) are a hazard needing control
expectations.evidence: 'Reasonably foreseeable use: consumers, including children, eat the dough raw'

expectations.text: Identifies a supply-chain preventive control for the supplier-applied heat treatment of flour (and/or pasteurized eggs), since there is no kill step in the facility
expectations.evidence: Flour and egg: 'Supply-chain-applied control', Subpart G program

expectations.text: Identifies food allergen controls for milk, egg, wheat, tree nuts (walnut) and soy if present: labeling control and cross-contact controls
expectations.evidence: 'Wheat, egg, milk, tree nuts (walnut), soy' allergen labeling and cross-contact controls

expectations.text: Identifies a process control for refrigeration/temperature (time-temperature) or notes the environmental pathogen hazard for exposed RTE product with sanitation control and environmental monitoring
expectations.evidence: 'Sanitation controls for RTE dough food-contact surfaces, plus environmental monitoring'; refrigeration process control if dough supports growth

expectations.text: States a recall plan is required because hazards requiring preventive controls were identified
expectations.evidence: 'Recall plan — Required, because you have HRPCs (117.139)'
